questions.question: Why is an HTTP success rate insufficient as the primary GenAI health signal?
options: A request can succeed technically while its answer, cost, latency, safety, or user outcome is unacceptable.
HTTP responses never include status codes for model requests.
Every successful request has exactly the same token cost.
Infrastructure metrics already contain the full prompt and response.
questions.explanation: Transport success covers only one layer; production health also depends on execution behavior and user-visible outcomes.

questions.question: A fleet groundedness score moves from 92% to 89.8%. What is the best next step?
options: Validate the measurement, compare bounded slices, and inspect representative traces before attributing a cause.
Immediately retrain the foundation model.
Ignore the movement because the aggregate remains above 80%.
Add request IDs as a Prometheus metric label.
questions.explanation: An aggregate movement detects change but does not identify the population or component responsible.

questions.question: Where should an unbounded request ID normally be recorded?
options: On a trace or controlled event record used for investigation.
As a label on every fleet-level metric series.
Only in a dashboard screenshot.
Inside the alert title with the raw prompt.
questions.explanation: Request IDs are valuable for correlation but create explosive metric cardinality when used as time-series labels.

questions.question: Which alert carries enough evidence to be actionable?
options: A predeclared boundary plus window, affected slice, representative traces, owner, response, and resolution condition.
A red dashboard tile with no denominator.
A single evaluator score with no version or sample count.
An hourly spend total with no traffic or success context.
questions.explanation: An actionable alert explains the boundary, population, evidence, and owned response instead of only reporting a number.

questions.question: A quality floor is breached, but the affected slice has sparse labels and the release has not been reproduced. What is the safest response?
options: Cap exposure and escalate evaluation rather than claiming a proven rollback cause.
Expand the rollout to gather traffic faster.
Delete the quality floor after seeing the result.
Average quality with lower cost and ship if the blended score improves.
questions.explanation: The breach matters, but weak coverage and attribution require bounded exposure and more evidence before a causal claim.

questions.question: Why should raw prompts, outputs, retrieved text, and tool arguments be opt-in telemetry?
options: They can contain personal, confidential, regulated, or security-sensitive data and need purpose, access, and retention controls.
They can never help reproduce a production failure.
OpenTelemetry forbids all string attributes.
Hashing always makes every identifier anonymous.
questions.explanation: Content can be diagnostically valuable, but collection must be minimized and protected according to the application's data obligations.
